rules.height_rules: In Bannau Brycheiniog National Park, even paving work can move into a closer review if it relies on raised height changes, retaining edges or platforms that materially change the site.
rules.depth_rules: Large impermeable areas in Bannau Brycheiniog National Park usually deserve the earliest drainage check, particularly where the work affects the front garden or main parking area.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary treatment, highway relationship and crossover changes often shape the hard-surfacing answer in Bannau Brycheiniog National Park more than the paving material alone.
rules.roof_rules: For hard-surface projects, the design equivalent of a roof check is usually the drainage fall and discharge strategy rather than any vertical structure.
rules.materials_rules: Permeable finishes and a softer overall frontage usually work better in Bannau Brycheiniog National Park than extensive impermeable paving with little visual relief.

restrictions.conservation_area: Hard surfacing in conservation areas within Bannau Brycheiniog National Park often faces a closer review where it changes the look of a visible frontage or removes established soft landscaping.
restrictions.listed_building: Works to the setting of a listed building in Bannau Brycheiniog National Park, including resurfacing and level changes, can need a more careful planning and heritage review.
